clue.text: Juggling trick, extremely skilful 8

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme ends of the word skilful, its first and last letters

parts.note: the figure 8 is spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: A juggler's trick rated as superbly skilful, scoring 8 out of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterous trickery, as in sleight of hand, the conjuror's or juggler's deceptive move.

clue.text: Starts to surprise indolent mates with exercises

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their opening letters

parts.note: to tup is to mate, said of a ram with a ewe

explanation.surface: Catching lazy friends off guard with a burst of physical training.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a farming word: a ram, and as a verb what a ram does with a ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are a familiar abdominal exercise, lying down and raising the torso.

clue.text: Spray a green bug on a large scale

indicators.note: spraying scatters something about, so the letters of a green are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to spray green paint on an insect, made large.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug is to annoy; doing it in a big way makes someone furious, a strong form of irritation.

clue.text: Give up crime in Oz, reportedly, and wield pen anonymously

indicators.note: Oz is Australia; the phrase is said in a broad Australian accent, where it comes out sounding like a different word

parts.note: a reformed criminal is said to go straight

explanation.surface: A criminal in Australia going straight and turning to anonymous writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is on the Australian accent, in which 'straight' sounds close to 'write' and 'go' close to 'ghost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter produces text published under someone else's name, writing without credit.

clue.text: Coach knocking back rough alcohol half-heartedly

indicators.note: the heart of the reversed word is two letters; dropping one of them leaves it half-hearted
knocking back usually means drinking, but here it sends the word backwards

parts.note: rotgut is slang for cheap harsh liquor

explanation.surface: A sports coach downing cheap booze without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' turns ROTGUT into TUGTOR; 'half-heartedly' removes one of its two central letters, the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor coaches a pupil, giving private instruction: the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Two women refused to grow up and wed as ordered

indicators.note: refused means the two letters are turned away and left out

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for woman, so two of them give two Ws

explanation.surface: Two women declined to mature and marry as they were told to.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Ws from GROWUPWED and the remaining letters already stand in the right order.
explanation.definitionFit: Things grouped are arranged or sorted together, so classified or ordered.

clue.text: Surveyor finally finding excuse to stop

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: to desist is to stop or cease

explanation.surface: A surveyor at last coming up with a reason to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks as if it governs only 'finding', but it takes the last letters of 'finding excuse to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A geodesist surveys and measures the shape of the earth, a specialist kind of surveyor.

clue.text: Stone axes one cut in advance

indicators.note: in advance means the shortened word goes in front of the axes
cut means the word one loses its last letter

parts.note: graph axes are labelled X and Y, here taken as the letters Y and X

explanation.surface: A stone axe-head, one of them trimmed beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious stone used in carving and jewellery.

clue.text: Professional lady accepting kiss with a lot of tongue

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: accepting means the name takes the kiss inside it

parts.note: Lily is a woman's name
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A working girl agreeing to a deep French kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a lot of tongue' reads as a racy kiss but means talking at great length.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking prolixly means wordily, using far too many words, so an excess of tongue in the sense of speech.

clue.text: Ditheringly dredge — and mostly in the wrong place

indicators.note: dithering is moving about indecisively, so the letters are shuffled about
mostly means the word and loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone dredging a channel haphazardly, mostly in the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims 'and' to AN, which joins DREDGE as the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged in its older sense means disarranged, put out of its proper order or position.

clue.text: Time loosely constituting something incomplete

parts.note: 'or so' means roughly or approximately, so loosely stated

explanation.surface: A rough timescale for a project that is still unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is a trunk without head or limbs, and figuratively a mutilated or unfinished work.

clue.text: It's used in building 8

definitions.meaning: a standard length of sawn timber two inches by four in section, used in carpentry
two multiplied by four equals eight

explanation.surface: Something used in construction, number 8.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber is named for its cross-section, and the phrase read as multiplication gives eight.

clue.text: Urge parent to circulate exciting book

indicators.note: circulating moves things round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pressing a mother or father to pass round a thrilling novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A compelling novel that keeps a reader eager to continue is called by this idiom.

clue.text: Seconds of pie and onions in pub

indicators.note: seconds of means the second letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Second helpings of pie and onions served in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like extra helpings of food; it means the second letter of pie, onions and in.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a public house, synonym for a pub, often with rooms.

clue.text: Keen on people chanting

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for crowds singing together.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonation is the reciting of a chant or liturgy in a singing voice, as when a priest intones.

clue.text: Colour of cat pee, formerly

indicators.note: formerly means the letter comes before the cat

parts.note: the letter P is pronounced pee
the Russian Blue is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: Asking what colour a cat's urine once was.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussian blue is a deep blue pigment, a dark ferric ferrocyanide dye named after Prussia.

clue.text: What if drinking carries no risks, ultimately?

indicators.note: carries means the drinking word holds the letters inside

parts.note: supping is drinking, sipping a drink

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of each of no and risks

explanation.surface: Wondering whether drinking might turn out harmless after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Both open a hypothetical, as in asking what would follow if something happened: an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Malcontent may scorn Oxfam, Unicef etc

indicators.note: malcontent suggests discontented or disordered, so the letters of may scorn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgruntled person may sneer at charities like Oxfam and Unicef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malcontent' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam and Unicef are names built from initial letters, so they are examples of abbreviation words.

clue.text: Be behind subordinate's false statement

parts.note: someone under another is subordinate to them
a lie is a false statement

explanation.surface: Being the source of a junior employee's untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: To underlie something is to lie at its root, to be the cause or basis behind it.

clue.text: It's treated by gastroenterologists, strangely, not opticians

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of not opticians are made odd by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A gut condition handled by specialists, oddly not by eye doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Constipation is a bowel complaint, the sort of digestive disorder that gut specialists treat.

clue.text: Couple adopting European design style

indicators.note: adopting means the joining word takes the letter into itself

parts.note: to hitch is to couple, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: A pair taking on a Continental look for their home.
explanation.definitionFit: High-tech is an interior and architectural style using industrial materials and exposed fittings.

clue.text: Livingstone perhaps keeping newt in lounge

indicators.note: keeping means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to lie about is to lounge
an eft is a newt, especially a young one

explanation.surface: An explorer keeping a newt in his sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: Livingstone is Ken Livingstone, the left-wing former Mayor of London, not the Victorian explorer, and Ken Livingstone was famous for keeping newts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Livingstone is a well-known socialist politician, an example of a left-winger.

clue.text: Be indebted to nameless Welshman

indicators.note: nameless removes N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Owen is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: Being in debt to an anonymous man from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe someone is to be indebted to them, whether for money or a favour.

clue.text: Travel round African country, northeastern gem

parts.note: to tour is to travel round a place
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A trip around an African nation in search of a gem from its northeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline mineral valued as a gemstone in many colours.

clue.text: It's essential to cure habit

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Treatment is vital to beating an addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'It's' as the definition, which cannot stand for a treatment; the whole clue defines it, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation treatment for addicts is the standard means of breaking a drug or drink dependency.

clue.text: Letter to Socrates written up in patois

indicators.note: in a down answer, written up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters lie inside the word patois

explanation.surface: A note to the philosopher composed in local dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides ATOI in 'patois'; 'written up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Socrates, an ancient Greek, would know.

clue.text: To show pain is hard and a bit cowardly

parts.note: to show pain one might yell
ow is the cry of someone hurt
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Crying out when hurt is tough and rather timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow means cowardly, and the -ish suffix tones it down to somewhat so.

clue.text: Still upset (but not very)

indicators.note: not says the letter for very is left out

parts.note: to invert is to upset, turn over

explanation.surface: Still a bit upset, though not greatly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but gives INVERT as a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, lacking movement, so the adjective still is a synonym.

clue.text: Told police about male meeting bishop for affair

indicators.note: about means the informing word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
he is a male pronoun
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An informer told the police about a man meeting a bishop for an illicit liaison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests a romance, but here it means a business or thing, as in the whole shebang.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang is a slang word for an affair or matter, used in the idiom 'the whole shebang'.

clue.text: Female entering, cause of misery

indicators.note: entering means the female word goes into the other

parts.note: a bane is a cause of ruin or misery
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman arrives who brings nothing but grief.
explanation.walkthrough: In Irish folklore this female spirit appears and wails before a death, so her arrival brings misery.
explanation.definitionFit: A banshee is a female spirit whose wailing foretells a death in the family, an omen of grief.
